coverage_note: Permits issued by the City of Orlando only. Orange County (unincorporated) permits run through a separate county system and are not in this feed; totals here are City of Orlando totals, labeled as such.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one permit_number in the City of Orlando's Permit Applications dataset, restricted to applications the city actually issued (issue_permit_date present). The dataset's grain is one row per permit application: no collapsing applies or is needed.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (issue_permit_date >= 2025-10-27), measured 2026-10-27: 28,424 rows = 28,424 distinct permit_number, 0 duplicates, 0 nulls. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: permit_address, as published (whitespace collapsed; all-caps values title-cased). The feed publishes no property ZIP code, so zip stays NULL.
field_map.application_date: processed_date (the date the city processed the application; present on 28,396 of 28,424 window permits).
field_map.category: plan_review_type, the city's own review class: 'Residential 1/2' and 'Residential 3 or more' = Residential (18,937 window permits), 'Commercial' = Commercial (9,486); the single 'No Plan Review Type' permit stays NULL.
field_map.contractor_rule: contractor_name ONLY — the permit's published contractor company of record (present on 27,176 of 28,424 window permits). The pull's column list never requests property_owner_name or parcel_owner_name (property-owner person names), contractor (the individual licensee-name field), contractor_address, contractor_phone_number, or private_provider_qualifier_name.
field_map.issue_date: issue_permit_date. The window is defined on it: a record enters this report when the city records an issue date — the dataset is an applications register, so applications never issued (145,096 all-time rows carry no issue date) are outside the population by definition.
field_map.permit_number: permit_number (unique in the window, see dedupe_rule).
field_map.permit_type: application_type, the city's own permit family naming (Building Permit, Electrical, Mechanical Permit, Plumbing, Engineering, Fire Permit, GAS, Demolition Permit, FloodPlain).
field_map.project_description: project_name, the city's own project label for the permit, as published.
field_map.status: application_status, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. Window statuses: Finaled 16,898 / Open 10,923 / Completed 378 / Closed 163 / Hold 55 / Hardhold 7 — every window record carries an issue date, so post-issuance states stay in the population (the Raleigh treatment).
field_map.valuation: estimated_cost, stored and published as reported. Measured on the full window (2026-10-27): stated on 28,424 of 28,424 permits (0 null), 2,371 at $0, only 18 at $1, 26,035 above $1; window total $2,953,602,837.65. No restatement pathology: a project's building and trade permits state different costs (e.g. the Tradeport hangar's building permit states $141,500,000 and its electrical permit $25,125,000 — its own slice, not the project figure repeated), only 3 permits state more than $100,000,000, and the largest ($210,000,000, a hospital medical-office building) is 7.1% of the total — the Chicago flagship shape. Repeated values are round-number estimates and identical buildings in one development stating the same estimate 2-3 times (worst-case repeated-value excess ~5% of the total, the Boston shape). VALUES PUBLISH; the DB window sum must reproduce the source-side total, and September 2026 must match the source exactly (2,035 permits / $122,131,123.57).

history_range: issue_permit_date 1907 onward in the source (legacy records); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: City of Orlando open-data terms (portal standard); attribution: City of Orlando, Florida
rate_limit: Socrata anonymous tier; paged at 5,000 rows/request with the adapter's 0.4s pacing. Note: the anonymous tier intermittently returns HTTP 403 on $where clauses containing text literals with spaces (measured during the audit) — the pipeline's date-only window clause is unaffected.
source_name: City of Orlando open data — Permit Applications
terms_status: verified-open-2026-10-27: the City of Orlando publishes this dataset on its open-data portal for public reuse; figures are published 'as reported by the City of Orlando' with attribution; no endorsement is implied (WAVE1 audit verdict READY, High confidence).
update_cadence: Daily (applications stream, continuous); MEASURED 2026-10-27: rowsUpdatedAt 2026-10-27T19:30:13Z (same day) and newest issue_permit_date 2026-10-27. Freshness (gate 5) is measured as the dataset's rowsUpdatedAt under a 48h threshold (the Socrata-county standard).
watermark_field: issue_permit_date + permit_number — refresh re-pulls by the issue_permit_date watermark and upserts.
